newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end with big losses, off lows.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end with big losses, off lows.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended sharply lower but off lows set during the morning's active selloff.
Traders said afternoon activity had dwindled from a brisk morning pace, which they figured still sufficed to pump up the day's volumes to substantial levels.

But prices clung to tight ranges following the morning's breakdown as players weighed U.S. jobs data that showed far more economic strength than expected and decided the statistics boded for higher U.S. interest rates during the first quarter to curb growth, increase the jobless rate and keep inflation at bay.

Nonfarm payrolls jumped 262,000 from an upwardly revised November and against average forecasts for a 192,000 increase. The jobless rate stood at 5.3 percent, matching forecasts and unchanged from the downwardly revised November rate.
Hourly earnings rose six cents, or 0.5 percent, to $12.05 from $11.99 and versus forecasts for a 0.2-percent rise. The average workweek rose to 34.8 compared to forecasts for unchanged at 34.5 hours.
The data jolted March Treasury bond futures, which skidded below support levels but managed to hold a retracement level at 109-24/32 and close above Thursday's low at 110-08/32.
But others called the contract's one-point-plus drop a poor technical performance that could keep bargain-hunters on the sidelines.
Some also suggested that those who have ready cash may be funneling some of it into the U.S. stock market, which rebounded from steep early losses Friday.

"I think there's some of that (asset allocation)," said one T-bond futures floor broker, noting the recovery in U.S. stocks. "If they've liquidated in the Treasury market, they have cash and that's (stock market) where it's going."
